title: Privacy notice linked from the home page
question: Can a visitor reach a privacy notice from the home page, and does it give a way to contact the business?
method: Take the privacy page found in the home page links or, failing that, a home page link whose label or path names privacy in the page language (privacy, Datenschutz, confidentialité, privacidad, privacidade, riservatezza, tratamiento de datos and the like), and read it. Found when the page loads and gives an email address or a postal address. Review when the page cannot be read or gives neither. Not found when no privacy link is found. Whether the notice names a company is recorded as evidence but does not change the verdict.

spec.title: California Online Privacy Protection Act, Bus. & Prof. Code §22577(b)

title: Privacy contact published
question: Does the privacy notice name a data protection officer or privacy officer with a way to reach them?
method: In the privacy notice, look for a named role (data protection officer, DPO, Datenschutzbeauftragter, délégué à la protection des données, encarregado, responsable de la protection des renseignements personnels, privacy officer and the like) with an email address within about 600 characters after it. Found when both are present. Review when the role has no email address near it, or when the notice gives an email address but names no role. Not found when the notice has neither. Skipped when no readable privacy notice was found. Not every business must appoint a DPO (data protection officer), but one that need not still needs a contact for privacy requests.

title: California opt-out links
question: Does the home page carry the opt-out links California prescribes for businesses that sell or share personal information?
method: Found when a link, button or image alt text on the home page says "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information", "Do Not Sell My Personal Information", "Your Privacy Choices", "Your California Privacy Choices" or "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information". The opt-out icon counts only when its alt text carries one of these phrases. Review otherwise, because businesses under the CCPA thresholds, or that neither sell nor share personal information, need no link. Runs when the store appears to sell in the United States.

title: Global Privacy Control declared
question: Does the store declare that it honours Global Privacy Control?
method: Fetch /.well-known/gpc.json. Found when it answers 200 with valid JSON and "gpc": true, or when the privacy notice mentions Global Privacy Control, GPC, Sec-GPC or an opt-out preference signal. Review when gpc.json says false or neither signal is present. GPC is a browser signal that asks a site not to sell or share the visitor's data. Whether a site honours it happens in the browser and cannot be checked without running JavaScript.

title: No advertising cookies or trackers before consent
question: Does the first response set advertising or analytics cookies, or load trackers without a consent block?
method: Read the Set-Cookie headers of the home page response and the script tags in its static HTML. Review when the server sets a known advertising cookie (`_fbp`, `_gcl_au`, `IDE`, `fr` and the like) or a known analytics cookie (`_ga` and the like) before any interaction, or when a tracker tag (Google tag, Meta pixel, TikTok, LinkedIn, Hotjar and the like) loads without a consent-blocking attribute. A Google tag also counts as blocked when an inline Consent Mode default sets storage to denied. Found (none seen) otherwise. Most trackers load through JavaScript, so a clean result means none were seen, never that consent works.

spec.title: UK Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003, regulation 6
